assessment.reason: The narrative review and proposal make EQ-5D-5L selection, validation, implementation, and utility reporting primary research objects. EQ-5D is not only an outcome or model input. The acknowledgement names university groups but does not link EuroQol support to the work.
source: Full article, EQ-5D DESCRIPTION, USES, CONVERSION TO HEALTH-UTILITY AND QALYS

studies.label: Conceptual proposal for EQ-5D-5L adoption and health-utility reporting in critical care
studies.family_rationale: The principal contribution is a completed conceptual proposal for wider EQ-5D-5L use, validation, and visualization in critical care. It proposes a workflow that reports health utility and mortality separately and as QALYs. It does not conduct an empirical validation or a systematic evidence synthesis.
source: Full article, HEALTH-UTILITY REPORTING ON SAME GRAPHS AS ESTABLISHED MORTALITY KAPLAN-MEIER CURVES

items.statement: Critical care studies have not routinely measured HRQoL, in part because some patients cannot complete patient-reported measures and some existing tools are burdensome.
source: Full article, HISTORY OF EXISTING HEALTH-RELATED QUALITY-OF-LIFE MEASUREMENT TOOLS IN CRITICAL CARE, paragraph 1

items.statement: The authors identify EQ-5D as the most promising current HRQoL tool for critical care because it is brief, covers low utility states, includes a health VAS, has translated versions, and supports country-specific scoring.
source: Full article, EQ-5D DESCRIPTION, USES, CONVERSION TO HEALTH-UTILITY AND QALYS, paragraphs 1-2

items.statement: An aggregate QALY result can conceal different contributions from survival and health utility, while disaggregated graphical reporting can show the outcome drivers.
source: Full article, HEALTH-UTILITY REPORTING ON SAME GRAPHS AS ESTABLISHED MORTALITY KAPLAN-MEIER CURVES, paragraphs 1-2 and Figures 1-2

items.statement: EQ-5D-5L patient and proxy versions should be validated as standardized HRQoL measures for critical care research.
Critical care studies should report health utility and mortality separately and also report their aggregated QALY result to support interpretation and decision-making.
source: Full article, HEALTH-UTILITY REPORTING ON SAME GRAPHS AS ESTABLISHED MORTALITY KAPLAN-MEIER CURVES, paragraph 2

items.statement: Patient incapacity can prevent self-report, patient and proxy ratings can differ, and retrospective baseline ratings can be affected by recall bias.
source: Full article, HRQOL IMPLEMENTATION AND MEASUREMENT, limitations paragraph

items.statement: Different HRQoL tools can assign different utilities to the same health state, and EQ-VAS ratings can differ from EQ-5D-5L algorithm scores.
source: Full article, EQ-5D DESCRIPTION, USES, CONVERSION TO HEALTH-UTILITY AND QALYS, paragraph 2
Full article, HRQOL IMPLEMENTATION AND MEASUREMENT, limitations paragraph

items.statement: Critical care QALYs can be skewed by mortality, the correct measurement horizon is uncertain, and longer follow-up increases loss to follow-up and incomplete data.
source: Full article, HRQOL IMPLEMENTATION AND MEASUREMENT, QALY challenges paragraph

items.label: Disaggregated QALY reporting
items.description: Report health utility and survival or mortality separately alongside the aggregated QALY result so that the drivers of the result remain visible.
source: Full article, HEALTH-UTILITY REPORTING ON SAME GRAPHS AS ESTABLISHED MORTALITY KAPLAN-MEIER CURVES

items.label: EQ-5D-5L as a proposed gold-standard critical care HRQoL tool
items.description: The authors propose focused validation and standardized use of patient and proxy EQ-5D versions in critical care.

items.evidence: The paper proposes graphical reporting of health utility alongside mortality on Kaplan-Meier curves, but the method-function vocabulary has no reporting or visualization value.
items.importance: This proposed reporting method is a principal contribution of the paper.
items.proposed_resolution: Consider a method function for reporting or visualization if this use recurs across studies.
source: Full article, HEALTH-UTILITY REPORTING ON SAME GRAPHS AS ESTABLISHED MORTALITY KAPLAN-MEIER CURVES
